correctness.rationale: Exact solution on each unit cell with sampled self-consistency z=q*y/(1+c*(1-q)) gives M0=r−uc and Mtheta=(r−wc)/(1+vc); the two-step multiplier P=M0*Mtheta governs all mesh states, with bounded within-cell propagation. Completing a square proves (1+vc)(P+r)=uw(c−r/u)^2+r(1+r)−wr²/u>0 for all c>=0,theta in [0,1]; so P>−r>−1. For theta<1, the strictly upward quadratic for P−1 has exactly one positive root c*, giving the iff stability region; at theta=1 w=0 and all finite gains stable. Both numerator factors vanish at c1=r/u and c2=r/w when 0<theta<1; the global trajectory vanishes from t=1 or t=2 respectively. As theta->1, w~alpha*r*(1−theta) and w*c*->1+r, hence (1−theta)g*->1+e^alpha. Rational case r=1/2,q=3/4 gives P=(1−c)(2−c)/(2(4+c)) with roots 1,2, threshold 6; independently checked by exact fractions.

value.rationale: A complete sharp gain-phase stability diagram, two finite-extinction gains and singular disappearance of the gain ceiling are motivated bifurcation phenomena for alternating advanced/retarded sampling. The facts distinguish simple one-period and endpoint cases and can inform hybrid-control theory without requiring a nonlinear generalization.

limitations: Only scalar linear inhibitory feedback, two equal-length cells and theta∈[0,1]. No nonlinear or arbitrary-mesh stability, no uniform rates as g->infinity.
